chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad) from Safwan from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sends a sacrificial animal (hady) as a voluntary offering. He said: 'He appoints a day for his companions in which they will mark/cut the ears of their animals. When that hour of that day arrives, he avoids what the Muhrim (one in Ihram) avoids. When the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) comes, it suffices for him. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the polytheists prevented him on the Day of Hudaybiyyah, he sacrificed a camel and returned to Medina.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: Sacrificial animal sent for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يُقَلِّدُونَ: They mark/cut (the ears of the animals)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for sending a sacrificial animal (hady) for Hajj in advance according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the ruling for voluntary sacrificial animals (hady) sent in advance, establishing that the sender assumes the state of Ihram restrictions from the moment the animal is marked until the Day of Sacrifice. It draws a direct parallel to the Prophet’s experience at Hudaybiyyah, where he was prevented from completing the Umrah and thus offered a sacrifice, thereby validating the practice of compensating for delayed or voluntary offerings through this specific ritual protocol.
